what: The whole workflow in one call
title: Step 4: Output and visualisation

Reach individual functions want tweak step; use biomes_full() want standard pipeline one call.

what: biomes: An R package for reproducible occurrence-to-biome classification using 31 global biome schemes
title: biomes: An R package for reproducible occurrence-to-biome classification using 31 global biome schemes
text: biomes ships spatially explicit raster layers 31 published global terrestrial biome schemes (compiled Fischer et al. 2022) one harmonised format, native 10 × 10 km resolution, together functions classify occurrence records biome classes choose suitable scheme dataset transparent, reproducible way. layers global 10 × 10 km, biomes built macroecological large-scale biogeographical questions (continental global). intended fine-grained, national-extent analyses, 10 × 10 km grid coarse. workflow follows four steps (see four vignettes ): Assembling occurrence records biome schemes. Choosing biome scheme: rank 31 schemes data. Occurrences--biome classification: assign records biome classes. Output visualisation: tabulate visualise result. single wrapper, biomes_full(), runs four steps one call.

title: biomes: An R package for reproducible occurrence-to-biome classification using 31 global biome schemes
text: biome scheme: one 31 published classification systems (e.g. vegetation scheme Ramankutty & Foley 1999). biome class: single category within scheme (e.g. savanna, tropical evergreen woodland). biome scheme number: number (1-31) identifies scheme; value pass scheme argument. Numbers follow order biome inventory (Fischer et al. 2022).

title: biomes: An R package for reproducible occurrence-to-biome classification using 31 global biome schemes
text: biomes_full() runs whole four-step workflow. Give occurrence dataset (taxon name); chooses best-fitting biome scheme, classifies records, tabulates , (optionally) builds figure. figure drawn default (plot = "none", fastest option). plot = "" returns combined figure res$plot, subset c("rank", "map", "barplot") returns panels individually (panel letters) res$rank, res$map res$barplot. force specific scheme, pass biome scheme number; rank within one methodological group, pass scheme type: pipeline individual building blocks, following four workflow steps: biomes_visualise() draws three panels (rank, map barplot) combined one figure; select subset panels, e.g. panels = "map".
code: library(biomes)  data(biomes_example)  # from an occurrence dataset: res <- biomes_full(x = biomes_example)   # scheme = "best"; no figure by default  res            # short summary res$scheme     # the chosen biome scheme number res$table      # occurrence records per biome class  # add a figure with `plot`; the combined figure is returned in res$plot: res <- biomes_full(x = biomes_example, plot = "all") res$plot ggplot2::ggsave("biomes_figure.png", res$plot, width = 9, height = 12, dpi = 300)  # the panels individually (no a/b/c letters) in res$rank / res$map / res$barplot: res <- biomes_full(x = biomes_example, plot = c("rank", "map", "barplot")) res$rank; res$map; res$barplot  # from a taxon name instead of a dataset (downloads from GBIF), e.g. a whole order: res <- biomes_full(taxon = "Fagales", plot = "all") biomes_full(x = biomes_example, scheme = 1)            # fixed scheme biomes_full(x = biomes_example, scheme = "vegetation") # best vegetation scheme # Step 1: Assembling occurrence records and biome schemes data(biomes_example) schemes <- biomes_get()  # Step 2: Choose a biome scheme ranking <- biomes_rank(biomes_example, scheme_type = "vegetation") best <- attr(ranking, "best_scheme")  # Step 3: Occurrences-to-biome classification cls <- biomes_classify(biomes_example, scheme = best)  # Step 4: Output & visualisation biomes_tab(cls) biomes_visualise(biomes_example, scheme = best)

what: Download the packaged biome raster stack — biomes_download
title: Download the packaged biome raster stack — biomes_download
text: 31-layer biome raster stack (Biomes_Inventory_RasterStack.tif, ~36 MB) large ship inside package CRAN. hosted release asset GitHub instead. biomes_download() fetches reuses local copy every later call, including every internal use biomes_get() biomes_classify().

title: Download the packaged biome raster stack — biomes_download
code: biomes_download(path = NULL, overwrite = FALSE, quiet = FALSE)

title: Download the packaged biome raster stack — biomes_download
text: path Optional character string: directory store raster. Default NULL: use persistent per-user cache directory user agreed , otherwise tempdir() (see Details). overwrite Logical flag; TRUE, re-download raster even local copy already exists. Defaults FALSE. quiet Logical flag; TRUE, suppress informational message download progress bar. Defaults FALSE.

title: Download the packaged biome raster stack — biomes_download
text: local file path raster, invisibly.

title: Download the packaged biome raster stack — biomes_download
text: storage location chosen follows: path supplied, raster written directory location touched. path NULL copy already exists persistent per-user cache directory (see tools::R_user_dir()), copy reused. Otherwise, interactive sessions, function asks permission store raster persistent per-user cache directory, download happens across R sessions. permission declined, non-interactive sessions, raster stored tempdir() removed automatically R session ends. package therefore never writes outside tempdir() without user's explicit consent (interactive confirmation explicit path).

title: Download the packaged biome raster stack — biomes_download
code: # \donttest{ # Downloads ~36 MB into the session's temporary directory. raster_path <- biomes_download(path = tempdir()) #> Downloading biome raster stack (~36 MB) to: #>   /tmp/Rtmpt3MgSm/Biomes_Inventory_RasterStack.tif raster_path #> [1] "/tmp/Rtmpt3MgSm/Biomes_Inventory_RasterStack.tif" # }

what: One-call workflow: from taxon (or dataset) to table (and optional figure) — biomes_full
title: One-call workflow: from taxon (or dataset) to table (and optional figure) — biomes_full
text: Convenience wrapper runs full biomes workflow single call. two entry paths:

title: One-call workflow: from taxon (or dataset) to table (and optional figure) — biomes_full
code: biomes_full(   x = NULL,   taxon = NULL,   scheme = "best",   lon = "decimalLongitude",   lat = "decimalLatitude",   value = "name",   plot = "none",   show = FALSE,   ... )

title: One-call workflow: from taxon (or dataset) to table (and optional figure) — biomes_full
text: x Optional. data frame longitude/latitude columns, sf spatial object, terra::SpatVector. Mutually exclusive taxon. taxon Optional scientific name (species, genus, family, ...). Mutually exclusive x. scheme One : integer 1:31 (biome scheme number) force specific scheme; "best" (default) pick best-fitting scheme across 31 via biomes_rank(); scheme type ("climate", "vegetation", "land_cover", "ecoregion", "integrative", "anthropogenic") pick best-fitting scheme within methodological group. lon, lat Column names longitude / latitude x (data frame ). Defaults "decimalLongitude"/"decimalLatitude". value Passed biomes_classify(): "name" (default), "ID", "". plot figure(s) biomes_visualise() build. "none" (default): figure (fastest option). "": combined, lettered figure (rank + map + barplot) $plot. subset c("rank", "map", "barplot"): requested panels returned individually (panel letters) $rank, $map $barplot – e.g. plot = c("rank", "map", "barplot") fills three, plot = "map" fills $map. NULL accepted alias "none". show Logical. TRUE, print figure () tabulation console side effect. function always returns result invisibly. Default: FALSE. ... arguments passed biomes_occ() taxon given (e.g. limit, year_min, year_max, use_download, GBIF credentials).

title: One-call workflow: from taxon (or dataset) to table (and optional figure) — biomes_full
text: Invisibly, biomes_full list elements: occ occurrence data frame (downloaded provided). scheme chosen biome scheme number. ranking ranking data frame (scheme = "best"), otherwise NULL. classified output biomes_classify(). table biome occurrence table biomes_tab(). plot combined, lettered figure (plot = ""), otherwise NULL. rank, map, barplot individual panels (letters), present requested via plot = c(...), otherwise NULL.

title: One-call workflow: from taxon (or dataset) to table (and optional figure) — biomes_full
text: taxon name. Pass scientific name taxon (x = NULL). biomes_full() calls biomes_occ() download cleaned GBIF occurrences taxon proceeds . occurrence dataset. Pass data frame, sf object terra::SpatVector x (taxon = NULL). occurrences available function: picks biome scheme (either scheme = <integer> , default scheme = "best", running biomes_rank() selecting top-1 scheme); classifies records biomes_classify(); tabulates biomes_tab(); optionally builds figure biomes_visualise() (controlled plot; skipped default speed).

title: One-call workflow: from taxon (or dataset) to table (and optional figure) — biomes_full
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Path 1: from a taxon name. Queries the GBIF web service and may # prompt for the download workflow (GBIF credentials), so it is not # run here. res <- biomes_full(taxon = "Fagus sylvatica", limit = 2000) res$table } # }  # \donttest{ # Path 2: from an existing data frame, pick the best scheme. # Uses the biome raster (~36 MB), downloaded on first use. data("biomes_example") res <- biomes_full(x = biomes_example, scheme = "best") #> biomes_full(): best scheme = 16 (Anthropogenic transformation of the biomes, 1700 to 2000)  # Path 2 with a fixed scheme res <- biomes_full(x = biomes_example, scheme = 1)  # Path 2, best-fitting scheme within the vegetation group, # and build the full figure res <- biomes_full(x = biomes_example, scheme = "vegetation", plot = "all") #> biomes_full(): best scheme = 9 (Defining functional biomes and monitoring their change globally) #> <SpatRaster> resampled to 5e+05 cells. res$plot   # individual panels (no a-c letters) in $rank / $map / $barplot res <- biomes_full(x = biomes_example, plot = c("map", "barplot")) #> biomes_full(): best scheme = 16 (Anthropogenic transformation of the biomes, 1700 to 2000) #> <SpatRaster> resampled to 5e+05 cells. res$map  res$barplot  # }

what: Internal package setup for biomes — biomes_globals
title: Internal package setup for biomes — biomes_globals
text: Reproducibly classifies occurrence records biome classes using 31 published global terrestrial biome schemes compiled Fischer colleagues (2022) doi:10.1111/geb.13574 , provided harmonised raster layers 10x10 km resolution globally. Includes functions choose suitable biome scheme dataset data-driven ranking, classify occurrence records, tabulate visualise result. Works user-provided occurrences taxon name, case occurrences downloaded GBIF (https://www.gbif.org) cleaned automatically.

Default "decimalLongitude". lat Column name latitude x (used x non-spatial data frame). Default "decimalLatitude". scheme_type Character. Restrict ranking one methodological group biome definitions: one "" (default; rank 31 layers), "climate", "vegetation", "land_cover", "ecoregion", "integrative", "anthropogenic". grouping taken scheme_type column biomes_information. specific type chosen, layers type classified, scored returned, scaled scores best layer determined within group. Ignored biome supplied. criteria Character vector one "coverage", "effective_classes", "granularity", "informativeness", "agreement". Default: first three. tiebreaker tied composite_scores resolved: "year" (default, recent publication ranks higher), "classes" (classes ranks higher), "none" (break ties; tied layers share rank, dense ranking). "year" "classes" key serves fallback, alphabetical scheme_name resolves remaining ties, ranks strict 1..N. "none" multiple layers may carry is_best = TRUE. verbose Logical. Print progress messages? Default TRUE.

title: Rank biome schemes for a given occurrence dataset — biomes_rank
text: data frame classes biomes_rank data.frame, one row per compared biome scheme. Columns: scheme (biome scheme number, 1-31), scheme_name, year (publication year scheme), n_total, n_hit n_na (number records total, classified, unclassified), pct_na (percentage unclassified records), one *_raw one *_scaled column per requested criterion (raw score min-max scaled version), composite_score (mean scaled criteria, drives ranking), rank (1 = best), is_best (TRUE top-ranked scheme). result carries attributes criteria, tiebreaker, scheme_type, best_scheme (biome scheme number top-ranked scheme, ready used scheme argument biomes_classify() biomes_full()).

title: Rank biome schemes for a given occurrence dataset — biomes_rank
text: default, three equally weighted criteria used: coverage: fraction records layer places biome (rest fall unclassified, NA cells). effective_classes: \(\exp(H')\) (Hill number order 1), .e. effective number biomes records spread across, weighted evenness. granularity: biome classes actually used, divided classes available layer. Two criteria can requested via criteria: informativeness: Pielou's evenness \(J' = H' / \log(k_{used})\). agreement: mean pairwise Cohen's \(\kappa\) layers (Monserud & Leemans 1992). raw scores min-max scaled \([0, 1]\) across compared layers averaged composite_score. Layers ordered score ties resolved according tiebreaker.

title: Rank biome schemes for a given occurrence dataset — biomes_rank
text: biomes_rank() gives data-driven ranking, authoritative "best" classification. criteria favour layers cover records split many, evenly-used classes, top-ranked layer necessarily suitable one question. best results, narrow comparison meaningful group via scheme_type, treat ranking shortlist rather verdict: inspect per-criterion columns result use biomes_info() choose layer whose definition resolution actually match data.

title: Visualise the biomes workflow (ranking, map and biome-class composition) — biomes_visualise
text: Produces publication figure biomes workflow set occurrence records. three panels drawn combined:

title: Visualise the biomes workflow (ranking, map and biome-class composition) — biomes_visualise
code: biomes_visualise(   x,   scheme = NULL,   scheme_type = "all",   biome = NULL,   lon = "decimalLongitude",   lat = "decimalLatitude",   panels = c("rank", "map", "barplot"),   legend_counts = TRUE,   legend = TRUE,   point_color = "#B20000",   point_size = 0.25,   combine = TRUE,   verbose = FALSE )

title: Visualise the biomes workflow (ranking, map and biome-class composition) — biomes_visualise
text: x data frame longitude/latitude columns, sf spatial object, terra::SpatVector point geometries. scheme Integer 1:31 (biome scheme number). NULL (default), best-fitting scheme chosen biomes_rank() (within scheme_type). scheme_type Character. Methodological group rank within scheme NULL; passed biomes_rank(). Default "". biome Optional single-layer terra::SpatRaster. supplied mapped directly map panel available (ranking). lon, lat Column names longitude / latitude x (data frame ). Defaults "decimalLongitude"/"decimalLatitude". panels Character vector, subset c("rank", "map", "barplot") (default three). Panels drawn lettered order. legend_counts Logical. TRUE (default), append number records per biome class map legend labels. legend Logical. TRUE (default), draw biome-class colour legend map panel. point_color Colour occurrence points. Default "#B20000". point_size Numeric size occurrence points. Default 0.25. combine Logical. one panel drawn: TRUE (default) combines one lettered figure (, b, c); FALSE returns named list individual panels (letters). Ignored single panel (always returned bare ggplot). verbose Logical. Passed biomes_rank(). Default FALSE.

title: Visualise the biomes workflow (ranking, map and biome-class composition) — biomes_visualise
text: single panel, ggplot object. several panels: combined cowplot object combine = TRUE (default), named list ggplot objects (rank, map, barplot) combine = FALSE. Print display save ggplot2::ggsave().

title: Visualise the biomes workflow (ranking, map and biome-class composition) — biomes_visualise
text: rank: data-driven ranking biome schemes (biomes_rank()): composite score per scheme (best highlighted) next raw criterion values averages (coverage, effective number classes, granularity, ...). map: occurrence records (points) mapped chosen biome scheme, number records per biome class optionally appended legend labels. barplot: number occurrence records (left) species (right) per biome class, biome-class names centre. panels drawn controlled panels; panel letters (, b, c) assigned drawing order, selecting rank barplot labels () (b).

title: Visualise the biomes workflow (ranking, map and biome-class composition) — biomes_visualise
code: # \donttest{ data("biomes_example") # full figure (rank + map + barplot), best scheme chosen automatically biomes_visualise(biomes_example) #> <SpatRaster> resampled to 5e+05 cells.   # only the map, for a fixed scheme biomes_visualise(biomes_example, scheme = 1, panels = "map") #> <SpatRaster> resampled to 5e+05 cells.   # map + barplot for the best vegetation scheme biomes_visualise(biomes_example, scheme_type = "vegetation",                  panels = c("map", "barplot")) #> <SpatRaster> resampled to 5e+05 cells.  # }

title: biomes 0.9.3
text: Initial CRAN submission. Provides raster layers 31 global biome schemes Fischer et al. (2022, Global Ecology Biogeography 31(11): 2172-2183) 10 x 10 km resolution globally. Terminology: schemes addressed biome scheme number (1-31). scheme argument biomes_classify(), biomes_rank(), biomes_visualise() biomes_full() replaces former layer argument; biomes_rank() returns columns scheme/scheme_name attribute best_scheme; biomes_tab() returns scheme column; biomes_information uses column scheme_number. Core functions: biomes_classify() (assign occurrence records biome classes), biomes_rank() (rank schemes coverage, effective number classes, granularity), biomes_tab() (tabulate records per biome class), biomes_visualise() (combined figure rank, map barplot panels, selectable via panels), biomes_full() (one-call wrapper), biomes_get() (load raster stack), biomes_info() (per-scheme metadata), biomes_occ() (optional GBIF download coordinate cleaning). biomes_visualise() now reproduces full workflow figure: rank panel shows composite score plus raw criteria averages (coverage, effective classes, granularity), map panel shows occurrence map (adaptive legend), barplot panel shows records species per biome class back--back centred labels. combine = FALSE individual panels returned named list instead one lettered figure. former biomes_show_rank() removed (ranking view rank panel). biomes_full(): scheme argument also accepts scheme type ("climate", "vegetation", "land_cover", "ecoregion", "integrative", "anthropogenic") pick best-fitting scheme within group, addition integer 1:31 "best". new plot argument controls figure(s) built: "none" (default, figure, fastest option), "" (combined lettered figure $plot), subset c("rank", "map", "barplot") (returned individually, without panel letters, $rank, $map $barplot). ~36 MB biome raster stack bundled inside package. hosted GitHub release asset downloaded per-user cache directory (tools::R_user_dir()) first use; biomes_download() performs (refreshes) download explicitly. keeps installed package well CRAN’s size limit. assembling occurrence records biome schemes, (2) choosing biome scheme, (3) occurrences--biome classification, (4) output visualisation.
